newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 12.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Thursday:
WASHINGTON - The District of Columbia Control Board will push the U.S. government to pay for about $1 billion worth of D.C. services to rescue the city from financial crisis.
WASHINGTON - Interactive museums, top-line retail developments serviced by a pedestrian walkway, underground parking and a street trolley system are envisaged for future downtown Washington.
WASHINGTON - Air force investigators have recommended no disciplinary action be taken against any officer in connection with the June truck bombing in Saudi Arabia that killed 19 U.S. airmen.

BRUSSELS - Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov agreed to NATO's offer of negotiations on a new charter to define post-Cold War relations between Moscow and the Western military alliance it long feared.

WASHINGTON - A coalition of Maryland religious leaders says it will not cooperate on the state's redesigned welfare programmes because its congregations cannot afford to assume the role the state envisions in providing services to the poor.

GREENSBORO, North Carolina - Food Lion, with 1,100 stores and more than 70,000 employees in 14 states, is suing ABC's "Prime Time Live," charging that the network used fraud, trespassing and other illegal means to to obtain footage showing workers doctoring spoiled meat and bleaching fish to remove unpleasant odours.
